newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS - Mixed views on Ayala Land Q1 net.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Mixed views on Ayala Land Q1 net.

text.p: Ayala Land Inc opened Manila's first-quarter reporting season on Tuesday by announcing a 15 percent rise in net income but analysts were mixed on what impact it would have on a market going through a downturn.
Philippine stocks have been under pressure in the past few days as investors sold property stocks on fears property prices could fall because of excess office and residential space.
Ayala Land said it posted a net income of 1.42 billion pesos ($53.99 million) for the first three months of the year, up from 1.24 billion pesos in the same period last year.

"It's disappointing because our expectation was 20 percent and this may not be reflective of the whole year. Instead of allaying fears, offhand, it may even worsen the perception of a property glut," said Cecilio de Castro, analyst at Anscor Hagedorn Securities.
But Sapphire Securities analyst Henry Ong said first-quarter earnings were higher than their 1.299 billion peso forecast.
"Somehow it will improve the bearish sentiment in the property sector," Ong said.

Another analyst believed otherwise. "Its too early to say if perception on the property sector will improve with this news, maybe on Ayala Land alone. We may have to wait for other property companies' earnings results," said Abacus Securities Corp analyst Raymond Franco.
Franco said Abacus would soon revise its income forecast for the company but could not say if there would be an upgrade or a downgrade.

An analyst from a big foreign brokerage house, who asked not to be named, said: "We are very happy that they came up with the figure. We may see a slight reversal in the market and a recovery on Ayala Land."
The analyst added that Ayala's first-quarter earnings were above the securities firm's 1.2 billion peso projection.
Citisecurities Inc research head Cilette Liboro said Ayala Land's result was higher than their projected 1.2 billion pesos.
She said if Ayala sustained the momentum of its first quarter income for the remaining three quarters of the year, the brokerage firm's 4.857 billion peso full-year profit forecast would be met.

"Everybody is looking at the cashflow of property companies stemming from rumours that Megaworld and Empire are suffering financial problems. Earnings wise, I think fears of investors on Ayala would be allayed," Liboro added.
Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc and housing subsidiary Empire East Land Holdings Inc shares have fallen sharply despite assurances from the two firms that talk of financial troubles were untrue.
Since March 1, the Philipine stock exchange's property sub-index has shed 214.52 points, or 13.25 percent, to 1,394.30 points.
The market's main index has taken a beating since February 3, falling from 3,447.60 points to 2,949.46 points, a drop of 498.14 points or 14.44 percent.
